hook.sub: + 6 more things AI power users know

tips.headline: Long chats make it *dumber.*
tips.why: 18 top models were tested. Every one got worse as the chat got longer.
tips.label: Hand it off
tips.prompt: Summarize this chat as a brief I can paste into a new chat.

tips.headline: It’s a *people-pleaser.*
tips.why: It learned from human ratings, and people rate agreement highly.
tips.label: Hide that it’s yours
tips.prompt: A classmate wrote this. Grade it harshly against this rubric.

tips.headline: It can’t see *letters.*
tips.why: It reads text in chunks called tokens, so it miscounts words and letters.
tips.label: Make it use code
tips.prompt: Use code to count the words in my essay.

tips.headline: You’re on the *wrong model.*
tips.why: Thinking modes work step by step before they answer. Use them for hard problems.
tips.label: Switch modes
tips.prompt: Model menu → Thinking (or Reasoning) for math, code and plans.

tips.headline: Document first. *Question last.*
tips.why: Paste the long text, then ask. Up to 30% better answers in tests.
tips.label: Order matters
tips.prompt: [paste the article]  Now: what are the 3 main risks?

tips.headline: Say what to do. *And why.*
tips.why: “Don’t” still plants the idea. A clear target plus a reason gets followed.
tips.label: Target + reason
tips.prompt: Explain it in 5 short sentences, because my grandma is reading it.

tips.headline: Make it *write the prompt.*
tips.why: It knows what it needs. Save the prompts that work and reuse them.
tips.label: After a great answer
tips.prompt: Write the prompt that would get this exact result in one shot.
